subject: Music Production
title: Dithering and Quiet Noise
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dithering and Quiet Noise.

hook.text: When producers reduce audio from 24-bit to 16-bit, they lose some of the quietest detail.

buildup.text: This reduction creates ugly distortion artifacts on the softest sounds in a recording.

discovery.text: Adding a tiny amount of random noise called dither masks those artifacts and smooths the sound.

twist.text: It seems backwards—adding noise actually makes the audio sound cleaner and more natural.

climax.text: Dithering is applied during mastering and is one of the final steps in professional production.

punchline.text: Adding noise makes quiet sounds cleaner.

quiz.question: What does dithering do in audio production?
options: Masks distortion artifacts by adding tiny random noise
